ui.ShieldCode — понятная проверка файлов са: ShieldCode — a clear check of website and app files before publishing.

ui.Все найденные проблемы, объяснения и при: All findings, explanations, and examples in one document.
ui.Начни с самых опасных проблем. Если испр: Start with the most serious issues. Safe automatic fixes are included in the project copy. Other recommendations are listed in the PDF plan. Review changes before replacing your original files.
ui.ShieldCode ищет известные шаблоны ошибок: ShieldCode looks for known patterns and may miss context. Review each finding; some matches may be harmless. No findings does not guarantee that a project is fully secure.
ui.Результаты прошлых проверок и сохранённы: Past scan results and saved reports.

ui.Выбери файлы или ZIP-архив. Поддерживают: Choose files or a ZIP archive. Code, settings, and dependency files are supported. Unsupported or oversized files are skipped.
ui.ShieldCode ищет знакомые ошибки: случайн: ShieldCode looks for common issues such as exposed passwords, unsafe data handling, and insecure settings.
ui.Для каждой находки указаны файл, место в: Each finding shows the file, location, and a suggested fix. Start with critical and high priority issues, then scan the project again.
ui.ShieldCode читает текстовые файлы и не з: ShieldCode reads text files and never runs your project. It does not check a published website, user access, or application logic. Scans can be wrong, and no findings does not guarantee security.
ui.Проверь найденный код и рекомендацию. Ес: Review the code and recommendation. If a real password or key was exposed, revoke it and create a new one.
ui.Разбери эти проблемы после срочных: пров: After urgent fixes, review data handling, settings, and app behavior.
ui.После этого — низкие и дополнительные: Then: low priority and extra tips
ui.Посмотри советы по улучшению. Некоторые: Review the improvement tips. Some matches may be expected in your project.

ui.Во время проверки выбранные файлы переда: During a scan, selected files are sent to the server running ShieldCode and processed in memory. When run locally, this is your computer. If hosted online, the service operator’s server processes them. Project code is not run. Original files are not written to the database or kept in scan history.
ui.В базе сохраняются имя загруженного объе: The database stores the uploaded item’s name, scan date, file count, score, findings, recommendations, dependency check results, and file snippets around findings. The scanner attempts to mask passwords and keys it recognizes in these snippets, but it may not detect every secret. Do not upload information that you cannot share with the service.
ui.Для работы аккаунта сохраняются имя поль: The account stores your username, selected language, and a salted password hash. Your password is not stored in readable form. A session cookie keeps you signed in for up to 7 days; use Sign out to end the session.
ui.Если в проекте найдены поддерживаемые фа: When supported dependency files are found, package names and exact versions are sent to the OSV online database to check for known issues. Project source code is not sent to OSV. This check runs automatically.
ui.В интерфейсе показываются последние 50 п: The interface displays the latest 50 scans, but this version does not have an automatic deletion period for older records. There is currently no self-service option to delete an account and all its history. Please consider this before uploading confidential projects.
ui.ShieldCode анализирует содержимое поддер: ShieldCode reviews supported files for known indicators of potential issues. It does not visit a published website or check its server, user permissions, or application behavior. No findings do not confirm complete security.

findingDescriptions.PRIVATE_KEY: A marker that looks like a private key was found. If it is real and the file was shared or published, treat the key as exposed.
findingDescriptions.CLOUD_KEY: This value looks like a cloud access key. Anyone who gets it may be able to access your cloud account.
findingDescriptions.HARDCODED_SECRET: A value assigned to a variable that looks secret was found. It may be a test value, so check it before taking action.
findingDescriptions.ENV_FILE_INCLUDED: Environment files often contain passwords and keys. They should not be published with a website or shared in a public repository.
findingDescriptions.EVAL: eval() runs text as code. If that text comes from a user or external source, unintended code may run.
findingDescriptions.NEW_FUNCTION: The Function constructor compiles text into executable code and can create risks similar to eval().
findingDescriptions.INNER_HTML: Adding an HTML string to a page can let someone inject code if the string includes user or external data.
findingDescriptions.DOCUMENT_WRITE: document.write() can insert content unsafely and may expose the page to injected code.
findingDescriptions.REACT_RAW_HTML: This option disables React's normal escaping. The HTML source must be carefully checked and cleaned first.
findingDescriptions.WILDCARD_CORS: The site allows requests from any website. Usually, access should be limited to trusted websites.
findingDescriptions.TOKEN_LOCAL_STORAGE: JavaScript on the page can read tokens stored here. A separate page issue could make them easier to steal.
findingDescriptions.TLS_VERIFY_DISABLED: Without certificate checks, the app may connect to an impostor website and expose data in transit.
findingDescriptions.COMMAND_EXEC: If user-provided data is included in this command, someone may make the app run unintended actions.
findingDescriptions.PY_SUBPROCESS_SHELL_TRUE: Running shell commands with user input can let someone change the command that is executed.
findingDescriptions.PICKLE_LOADS: Opening a pickle file from an untrusted source can run code stored inside it.
findingDescriptions.SQL_CONCAT: If user input is added directly to a database query, it may change the query and expose or alter data.
findingDescriptions.JWT_VERIFY_DISABLED: The app should verify the signature of each sign-in token. Without this check, a fake token may be accepted.
findingDescriptions.OPEN_REDIRECT: A link may be used to quietly send someone to a fake or unexpected website.
findingDescriptions.SSRF_SUSPECT: If a user controls the address, the app may reach internal services that should not be accessible from outside.
findingDescriptions.PATH_TRAVERSAL: If user input controls a file path, the app may read or change files outside the intended folder.
findingDescriptions.CSP_UNSAFE_INLINE: This setting weakens the page's protection against running injected code.
findingDescriptions.SRI_MISSING: Without an integrity check, the app cannot detect if an external script was replaced.
findingDescriptions.COOKIE_SAMESITE_NONE: This setting allows the browser to send sign-in cookies with requests to other websites.
findingDescriptions.XML_EXTERNAL_ENTITY: Some XML input can make an app read computer files or contact internal addresses.
findingDescriptions.HTTP_URL: An HTTP address sends data without encryption. Local addresses and documentation examples may be harmless.
findingDescriptions.OSV_DEPENDENCY: The online database lists a known issue for this library version. Review the details and update to a fixed version if one is available.

findingFixes.PRIVATE_KEY: If this is a real key, revoke it and create a replacement. Keep the new key outside the project files, such as in a protected environment setting.
findingFixes.CLOUD_KEY: Revoke the exposed key in your cloud account and create a new one with only the access the app needs. Store it outside the source files.
findingFixes.HARDCODED_SECRET: Move the secret to a protected environment setting. If it was published or shared, revoke it and create a new one.
findingFixes.ENV_FILE_INCLUDED: Keep the file out of public project folders and version control. Store real secrets in protected environment settings instead.
findingFixes.EVAL: Avoid eval(). Parse structured data with JSON.parse() or use explicit, predefined logic instead.
findingFixes.NEW_FUNCTION: Do not compile executable code from untrusted text. Use predefined functions and explicitly allowed actions.
findingFixes.INNER_HTML: Use textContent for plain text. If HTML is required, clean it with a trusted sanitizer and allow only needed elements.
findingFixes.DOCUMENT_WRITE: Create page elements and set plain text with textContent instead of using document.write().
findingFixes.REACT_RAW_HTML: Prefer normal text rendering. If HTML is required, sanitize it with a trusted library and never insert unchecked input.
findingFixes.WILDCARD_CORS: Allow only specific trusted websites. Do not combine unrestricted access with credentials.
findingFixes.TOKEN_LOCAL_STORAGE: For web sessions, consider server-managed cookies with HttpOnly, Secure, and an appropriate SameSite setting. Avoid long-lived secrets in browser storage.
findingFixes.TLS_VERIFY_DISABLED: Turn certificate verification back on and fix the certificate configuration instead of bypassing the check.
findingFixes.COMMAND_EXEC: Avoid passing user input to a shell. Use a safe API with separate arguments and validate each allowed value.
findingFixes.PY_SUBPROCESS_SHELL_TRUE: Avoid shell=True for commands containing user input. Pass a list of arguments and validate the accepted values.
findingFixes.PICKLE_LOADS: Do not load pickle data from untrusted sources. Use a data-only format such as JSON when possible.
findingFixes.SQL_CONCAT: Use parameterized database queries so user input is treated as data, not as part of the query.
findingFixes.JWT_VERIFY_DISABLED: Verify the token signature, allowed algorithm, issuer, audience, and expiry before accepting it.
findingFixes.OPEN_REDIRECT: Allow redirects only to a fixed list of trusted destinations or to relative paths on your own site.
findingFixes.SSRF_SUSPECT: Allow only required destinations. Block private network addresses and validate each redirect before connecting.
findingFixes.PATH_TRAVERSAL: Resolve paths inside the intended folder and reject any path that escapes it. Do not trust a user-supplied path directly.
findingFixes.CSP_UNSAFE_INLINE: Remove unsafe inline allowances where possible. Use a strict policy with nonces or hashes for required scripts.
findingFixes.SRI_MISSING: Add an integrity hash and cross-origin setting to the external script, or host a reviewed copy yourself.
findingFixes.COOKIE_SAMESITE_NONE: Use a stricter SameSite setting unless cross-site cookies are required; also enable Secure and HttpOnly where appropriate.
findingFixes.XML_EXTERNAL_ENTITY: Disable external entities and external document type definitions in the XML parser.
findingFixes.HTTP_URL: Use HTTPS for public services. Keep HTTP only for local development or documented cases where encryption is not needed.
findingFixes.OSV_DEPENDENCY: Check the library's release notes and upgrade to a version that fixes the reported issue. Test the app after updating.

findingDefaults.description: This code pattern may create a security or reliability risk. Check the surrounding code and confirm that user input and sensitive data are handled safely.
findingDefaults.fix: Review the code at this location. Follow the recommendation, restrict access to what the feature needs, and scan the project again after making changes.
